title: Readiness result
description: Whether a workload is ready to be observed by an agent, and on what evidence. Separate from the assessment result because the questions differ: readiness is about whether the framework can observe at all, and assessment is about what was observed. Merging them would let a readiness failure be reported as a health finding, which would blame the workload for the framework's inability to see it.

scopeContractHash.description: The scope readiness was evaluated against.

evidenceManifestHash.description: The canonical hash of the manifest backing this result.

checks.description: Required, and required even when empty. A readiness result with no checks performed is reporting that nothing was verified, which is the opposite of ready and must be readable as such.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this schema the instance conforms to (FR-05, FR-29).

identifier.description: Lowercase, hyphen-separated. Constrained so an identifier cannot carry arbitrary text, and English by construction (FR-03, CON-01).

opaqueId.description: An opaque handle, or a placeholder in the angle-bracket form that every shipped example uses.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339, UTC, Z-suffixed. The pattern is present because format is an annotation by default.

sha256Hex.description: Lowercase hex, exactly 64 characters, as ADR-0004 pins.

readinessStatus.description: Ready with findings is distinct from ready. Collapsing the two would discard the only signal that something needs attention before it becomes a failure, and collapsing it into not-ready would block a workload that can in fact be observed.

confidence.description: How much weight the status carries.

outcome.description: Not evaluated is distinct from passed and from not applicable. A check that never ran must not be counted towards readiness, which is exactly what happens when the only available values are pass and fail.

evidenceRefs.description: Entry identifiers in the backing evidence manifest.

remediationHint.description: What an operator would do about a failed check. A hint for a person, never an instruction for the agent: the framework proposes no action and executes none.
